checks: The positive-coefficient combination of an interior lift and a lift from farther along the projected line is an interior lift of the specified projected point. Translating by a vector in E-perpendicular preserves all cap inequalities and section planes, the projected centroids and the Hausdorff measures; it puts the origin in the interior and all specified cuts have positive section measure.

Fiber inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski give power concavity and positive density on the projection interior. The projection boundary is planar null and each ray from the interior origin meets it only at its endpoint. Replacing its values by zero leaves the planar, line and radial moments unchanged and keeps the positive set open and convex. Boundedness and integrability follow from compactness of K and boundedness of its fibers.

Fubini in E⊕E-perpendicular proves mass and cap preservation at the density stage. Applying Fubini within each fixed section separately uses the orthogonal sum (E∩uᵢ-perpendicular)⊕E-perpendicular, with Jacobian one, so both its mass and vector first moment projected to E are exact for every specified normal. In particular, the line first moment is zero; no perpendicular centroid coordinates or exceptional directions enter.

The extended inverse power is convex by decreasing convex composition with the positive concave root. The radial construction with r=2 and β=4 gives a convex body with exactly the stated cap fractions and area V. The line moment identity yields equal positive ray first moments I, hence radii sqrt(2I) and total centered chord length 2sqrt(2I). For m=d−2 the sharp lower line ratio becomes sqrt(d/[2(d−1)]), with upper ratio one.

The weights λᵢ proportional to θᵢrᵢ balance the oriented chords since rᵢLᵢ=Sᵢ/sqrt(f(0)); rotation maps their signed endpoints back to positive multiples of the original normals. Reweighting λ by 1/rᵢ gives θ exactly and all multipliers are in [1,b_d]. For d=2 a centered section is already a bisected chord of K; the original weights balance the endpoints and give 4/9 directly.

The squared comparison 2(d−1)/d≤16/9 is equivalent to d≤9; 3/7−27/64=3/448>0. Both terms in the maximum are strictly below 3/2 for d≥10, and 2·7⁶−5·6⁶=2018>0. The function x log(x/(x+1)) strictly decreases by log(1+t)>t/(1+t) for t>0, proving the gamma comparison in both ranges. At d=2, 4/9 is exactly gamma₂.

In the corollary zero weights can be dropped before choosing the span. Rank two supplies E, with an interior projected origin and projected centroids zero. Rank one has only two orientations, their common proper section measure is positive, and balance gives weight 1/2 to each. The two caps are complementary in volume, including d=1, where the section is the origin with H⁰ mass one. Rank zero is impossible for normalized weights on unit normals.
